newsitem.title: JAPAN: US focus on Japan trade due to lack of issues-MITI.
newsitem.headline: US focus on Japan trade due to lack of issues-MITI.

text.p: Trade Minister Shinji Sato said on Tuesday that U.S. officials are expressing concern about Japan's rising trade surplus because the United States has no major problems at home to worry about.
He made the remarks at a news conference where he was commenting on recent concerns expressed by U.S. officials about a recent rise in Japanese exports.

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said last Friday that she is concerned that Japan may be taking advantage of U.S. markets to export its way out of recession. Japan's trade surplus rose in February for the first time in two years.
"It (U.S. concern about Japan's trade surplus) is a reflection of the absence of major problems in the United States," Sato said.

He said the rise in Japan's trade surplus in February was due to the small size of the surplus in the same month last year and to the strength of the U.S. economy. "The rise was due to seasonal and temporary factors," he said.

Referring to a bilateral dispute over the paper trade, Sato said Japan neither plans to extend the 1992 agreement nor sign a new agreement. The aim of the 1992 accord is to promote Japan's purchase of foreign paper products.
The United States has called on Japan to sign a new agreement with the 1992 accord set to expire on April 4.
"Japan's paper market is open... I don't think there is anything to talk about," he added.
